subject: science
domain: Motion and Stability: Forces and Interactions
skillName: Patterns of Motion Predict Future Motion

items.prompt: Do many objects move in repeating patterns?

steps: Swings, clocks, and pendulums move in repeating patterns.

items.prompt: A swing takes the same time each back-and-forth. Can you predict its next swing?

steps: The repeating pattern lets you predict the next swing.

items.prompt: Name one object that moves in a repeating pattern.
items.answer: A swing (or clock hands, or a pendulum)

steps: Swings and clock hands repeat their motion.

items.prompt: Why can a pattern of motion predict future motion?
items.answer: Because the motion repeats the same way

steps: A repeating pattern keeps happening, so the next motion matches it.

items.prompt: A ball rolls the same path three times. What path will the fourth roll take?

steps: The repeating pattern means the fourth roll matches the others.

items.prompt: A pendulum swings 10 times in 20 seconds. About how many times in 40 seconds?

steps: Twice the time gives about twice the swings at a steady rate.

items.prompt: A toy train loops in 15 seconds each time. Where is it after 30 seconds?
items.answer: Back at the start (after two loops)

steps: Two loops in 30 seconds return it to the start.

items.prompt: True or false: a repeating motion makes it easier to predict the future motion.
If a clock's second hand takes 60 seconds to go around, where is it after another 60 seconds?

steps: The steady pattern returns it to the start each minute.

items.prompt: What should you observe or measure to find a pattern of motion?
items.answer: How the motion repeats and how long each repeat takes

steps: Observing the repeating motion and its timing reveals the pattern.

items.prompt: Explain how measuring a swing's timing helps you predict when it returns.
items.answer: If each swing takes the same time, you can predict the return time by the steady timing

steps: A constant swing time lets you predict each return.

items.prompt: A bouncing ball bounces a little lower each time in a steady pattern. How could you predict the next bounce height?
items.answer: Use the steady pattern of decreasing height to estimate the next bounce

steps: A regular decrease lets you predict the next height.

items.prompt: Why is a single random movement harder to predict than a repeating pattern?
items.answer: A random movement does not repeat, so there is no pattern to follow

steps: Without a repeating pattern, there is nothing reliable to predict from.

items.prompt: Describe how to use a pendulum's pattern to predict its position in the future.
items.answer: Measure its steady swing time, then use it to figure out where it will be later

steps: The steady swing time lets you project the pendulum's future position.

items.prompt: A merry-go-round turns once every 10 seconds. Predict how many turns in 1 minute and explain.
items.answer: 6 turns, because 60 seconds divided by 10 seconds per turn is 6

steps: At a steady 10 seconds per turn, 60 seconds gives 6 turns.
